Great! I moved the Geant4 material tracks to the storage folder in the top level directory, which has now the the older reference files and the newer one with less service material.



Also PR #112 got merged with a color schema:

- what I need now is: material_mapping for the new baseline 



Two stacked plots Geant4: 

- old baseline (beampipe, pixel, short strips, long strips - the detectors split in sensitive and passive, the latter shown by 50% opaque)
- new baseline (same colors)



Both plots should show the reconstruction/ACTS material as black markers and a ratio to the total Geant4 underneath, best using `unrooted` - the new baseline should also show a dotted line representing the old baseline (for total and short strip material) to illustrate the saving from the new readout scheme and reduced services.

I’ll identify the old and new recordings in `storage`, check the merged color scheme, and build the new ACTS material map. Then I’ll produce the two stacked comparisons with ACTS markers and ratio panels, using `unrooted` where it supports the required plotting.

The Spack registry still reports stale setup fingerprints and unverified full sources; I’ll recheck the actual runtime before running mapping. I’ll also verify the recording’s geometry identity: changing readout pitch alone does not remove physical material, so the savings comparison needs to identify which service changes the new file contains.

I found a provenance mismatch: the new file’s metrics point to the PR #109 compact, before PR #110’s reduced-service geometry. I’ll preserve both supplied files, use the 2 mm file as an intermediate control, and generate a separate current-baseline scan for the reduced-service comparison. The old and current baselines also differ in pixel layout, so I’ll distinguish the total change from the short-strip change.

The current-baseline scan is running successfully with the persistent `beamOn()` fix. I’m using the common range −4 < η < 4 for both plots, with the PR #112 colors and 50% opacity for passive material. The fresh geometry export for ACTS mapping is also underway.

The fresh scan completed: 100,000 geantinos, with one Geant4 run initialization and no aborts. ACTS mapping is now processing those tracks. I’m also checking the Geant4 component assignment and budget closure before drawing the sensitive/passive stacks.

The first checks found a boundary issue near some thin endcap cooling tubes: Geant4 records zero-length titanium crossings, and a few nearby steps disagree with the TGeo material lookup. I’m checking the affected material budget and whether ACTS drops only zero-length steps before accepting the map and plots.

ACTS accounts for the step-count difference exactly: it omits 185 zero-length slabs, with no loss of nonzero slabs or material budget on any ray. I’m now checking the remaining TGeo discrepancies against Geant4’s own geometry to resolve the component assignment.

The new ACTS map passes conservation and reload checks. The supplied PR #109 scan and the fresh scan also use exactly the same 100,000 rays: the full short-strip redesign reduces their mean radiation-length budget by 10.4%. That comparison includes the module, cooling and service changes; it does not isolate cables alone.

Geant4 resolves all 149 disputed steps to passive graphite pickup pieces, matching the recorded material. TGeo finds titanium at those same positions. I’ll retain that discrepancy in the report and use the audited Geant4 assignment for these steps. The 100,000-ray ACTS validation has also completed.

The comparison code now covers both radiation and interaction lengths, with a ratio panel beneath each. I’m finishing the audited component checks and figure rendering. The report will distinguish the total old-to-new baseline change from the PR #109-to-current redesign change.

The audited classification passes with no unassigned steps or unresolved material mismatches, and the figures are rendering. Over the common η range, the new baseline has 7.2% less total radiation-length material and 27.7% less short-strip material. Its total interaction-length budget is 2.9% higher, with the changed pixel baseline contributing to that increase.

Both figures are rendered and visually checked. I’m packaging the map, plots and reproduction commands, and arranging a separate review of the final numerical evidence. The report retains the Geant4/TGeo conversion issue and the map’s azimuthal-averaging and material-locality limits.

The map and fresh tracks are saved in `storage/nodd-tracker-des043-current`; both supplied files are unchanged. The separate review found one wording correction: I’ll label the old sample simply “validation rays,” since its original recording seed is unknown. This does not change the numerical results.
Really nice, but remove the old short strip dotted line from the new base-line, only keep the old-style Geant4 total
I’ll remove the old short-strip dotted line and keep the old Geant4 total on the new-baseline plot.
The revised PNG, PDF and SVG now keep only the dotted old Geant4 total. I’ve checked the updated figure visually, and all 17 checks pass. I’m finishing the review record.

Updated: the new-baseline plot now keeps only the dotted old Geant4 total. PNG, PDF and SVG regenerated; all 17 checks pass.

![Updated new-baseline plot]([redacted]

[PDF]([redacted]

I’ll use the sensitive detector crossings from the same old and new scans to plot hits versus η, with both stacked and individual-marker versions. I’ll check the hit definition against the recorded steps first.

I’ll define a hit as one distinct sensitive sensor crossed by a ray, so multiple Geant4 steps in one sensor count once. Each plot option will show old and new baselines side by side in the same colors. The environment preflight still reports stale setup records; I’ll verify the loaded runtime before processing.

The material files don’t store sensor identities, and rounded positions can be ambiguous at active/guard boundaries. I’ll count crossings directly from Geant4’s physical-volume paths in matched old/new runs. That gives each sensor a clear identity and avoids treating tiny or repeated material steps as extra hits.

The 300-ray control passed: adding the hit counter leaves all 32 material-recording branches exactly unchanged. It also verified all 46,682 sensitive placements in the new geometry. I’m now running 100,000 matched rays through each baseline.

The independent check agrees with Geant4 for 128 rays when it uses the sensors’ full thickness. A zero-thickness plane check misses a few edge-grazing crossings, so I’ll label the plots as sensitive-volume crossings rather than ACTS plane hits.

Both runs completed successfully, with identical generated rays. The mean count is 14.07 crossings per ray for the old baseline and 14.93 for the new one. Independent finite-sensor checks agree with Geant4 for 256 rays from each baseline. I’m rendering both plot options now.

Both plot options are rendered and checked visually. Pixels account for most of the increase; long-strip counts match exactly for every paired ray. I’m packaging the plots, binwise data and reproduction recipe, then getting a separate review of the results.

All 5 new checks pass, and the 17 existing material-comparison checks still pass. PNG, PDF and SVG exports are ready for both formats; the original material files are unchanged. I’m finishing the validation record.

Done—old baseline on the left, new on the right. Hits are distinct sensitive-volume crossings per ray, using 100,000 matched rays per baseline.

[Stacked + total markers — PDF]([redacted]

![Stacked hits]([redacted]

[Individual markers + total markers — PDF]([redacted]

![Individual hit markers]([redacted]
Now can you also run Fatras single muon resolutions 1, 5, 10, 100 comparing track parameters of old and new baseline - using truth tracking

I’ll set up a matched old/new Fatras truth-tracking comparison at 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV, using the existing reconstruction and resolution definitions. I’ll check the baseline inputs and run a small control before starting the full samples.

I’ll treat these as fixed pT values in GeV, with the established 3 T field and η range −4 to 4. The new baseline also needs hit-error calibration for its 2 mm strixels. I’ll check that independently before the fits. The environment registry still flags stale setup records, so the native control will verify the runtime directly.

The controls pass: all 100 old-baseline muons at 5 GeV fit successfully, and the new-baseline measurement-training pilot completed with its matching geometry and material map. I’m starting the full calibration and resolution samples, using the same truth-tracking chain for both baselines.

The new 2 mm calibration is complete and covers every measured sensor coordinate. The first full sample, old baseline at 1 GeV, also reproduces the previous run’s generated particles and fitted parameters exactly. The remaining cases are running; I’ll report fit losses and wrong-charge fits alongside the resolutions.

Both baselines have finished at 1 and 5 GeV; the 10 and 100 GeV samples are running. The first comparison shows mixed changes across track parameters. I’m keeping the full residual distributions and fit-loss accounting so the core-resolution plots can be interpreted properly.

The old 1 GeV sample reproduces the previous fitted parameters exactly. Centrally, the new baseline has a slightly narrower d₀ core, while its relative-pT core is about 13% wider. I’ll include an overview of new/old ratios alongside the per-momentum plots to make those tradeoffs visible.

The independent methodology review found no blocker to continuing. The analysis explicitly audits each case’s calibration and keeps failed or unavailable fits in the generated-event accounting. The old 10 GeV run is also complete; the remaining runs are progressing normally.

Both 10 GeV samples are complete. All eight samples were started fresh with the same frozen simulation and fit code; the 100 GeV pair is finishing now. The final plots will compare d₀, z₀, φ, θ, q/p and relative pT versus |η|, with fit-loss and charge-sign diagnostics alongside them.

The old 100 GeV run also reproduces its previous result exactly. It has substantial forward momentum tails and some wrong-charge fits, so a core width alone would be incomplete. Those outcomes remain in the comparison, and the report will show the full RMS and charge-sign counts. Only the new 100 GeV run remains.

The last sample has reached 19,000 of 20,000 events. Once it closes, I’ll check the output hashes, produce the final plots and get an independent check of the results. The forward 100 GeV diagnostics will stay visible alongside the core widths.

All eight runs are complete, and the final source, input, calibration and output checks pass. Centrally, the new baseline has narrower d₀ cores and wider relative-pT cores at all four momenta. I’ve produced the plots, ratio overview and full accounting report; they’re now ready for the independent results review.

Across the eight samples, 159,985 of 160,000 generated muons passed selection and produced finite fits; no attempted fit failed or returned invalid covariance. At 100 GeV, the charge-sign and tail diagnostics qualify the core-resolution comparison. The independent review is checking those details against the full ROOT samples and plots.

The independent review has reproduced the raw-data statistics and checked pairing, calibration variances, representative bootstrap intervals and all six plots. No material blocker has been found. The report also makes clear that the narrower new forward 100 GeV core comes with a much larger full RMS in this sample.

The independent review is complete and found no delivery blocker for this prototype comparison. It reproduced the full-sample statistics and calibration checks, including the forward-tail caveat. I’m recording the review and closing the reproducibility records; the plotted data are unchanged.

Completed **20,000 muons per baseline at fixed pT = 1, 5, 10, 100 GeV**, using Fatras truth tracking in 3 T.

Plots compare d₀, z₀, φ, θ, q/p and relative pT versus |η|:

[1 GeV]([redacted] · [5 GeV]([redacted] · [10 GeV]([redacted] · [100 GeV]([redacted]

Central d₀ improves; central relative-pT cores widen by roughly 6–13%. Forward at 100 GeV, the new core narrows while the full RMS grows substantially.

Eight tests and independent review passed. [Report, diagnostics and reproduction recipe]([redacted]

![New/old resolution ratios]([redacted]

Please make a PR out of this - it confirms the 2 mm to be good.

Record the new material map.
Accounting and merge preparation.

I’ll prepare the PR with the material map, comparison plots, accounting and required checks. I’ll keep the performance claim qualified: the 2 mm baseline has mixed resolution changes, including the forward high-pT tails.

The branch contains the material-map, hit-count and Fatras studies, and it is current with `main`. I’ll include all three in the PR and add a clear map record bound to the geometry and file hashes. I’ve also found the completed chat turns for accounting; the app’s current response does not expose token counters.

The 32 focused tests pass, the map record matches the native evidence, and all three plot sets replay successfully. I’ve added those checks to CI. I’ll now open the PR, attach the interaction/accounting record and verify the final head’s checks and merge status.
The GitHub connector cannot create pull requests with its current permissions. I’m using the authenticated repository CLI to open the PR and complete the accounting capture.

[PR #113 is open](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/113). The separate review found no actionable issues in the new map record, verifier or CI changes. I’m attaching the recovered interactions and accounting now, then checking CI before marking it ready for review.

I’ll read the assignment, then implement and run the mapping workflow with the specified current geometry and recording. I’ll keep outputs local and distinguish the earlier PR #109 recording from the current baseline.

The workflow is implemented, and all seven identity and count checks pass. The first native export found missing DD4hep component registry files beside the fresh factories. I’ve reported that build prerequisite to the coordinator and kept the loader guard intact. The existing native sidecar’s source, binary hash and ABI match retained successful run evidence.

The fresh native export passed: 46,682 sensor planes, 120 volumes and an exact JSON round trip. The unchanged binning policy selects 67 current portals with 8,650 bins. Mapping is now running on the completed 100,000-geantino recording, whose compact and factory hashes match this export.

The mapping audit found 185 exact zero-length slabs that the pinned ACTS ROOT reader omits. I’ve preserved the failed legacy audit and added explicit accounting for the reader’s zero-length omissions without changing the historical guard.

The separate seed-43 validation produced 100,000 rays, and the output check confirmed every starting vertex is at the origin. The reports, payloads and failed-control evidence remain under the local build directory.

pull_request.head: codex/baseline-material-comparison
pull_request.body:
Record the current 2 mm, reduced-service DES043 tracker material map and the old/new baseline comparisons used to assess the choice.

The retained map has **67 keyed portals and 8,650 averaged material bins**, bound to geometry `62f6056`, its compact/material/five factories, portal selection and exact map hashes. It was trained with 100,000 Geant4 geantinos and checked with 100,000 independent ACTS rays. The [map record](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-material-comparison/material-map-record.json) and [compressed map](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-material-comparison/material_map.json.gz) are included; full event samples remain local and ignored.

This PR also delivers:

- [Geant4 material stacks and ACTS ratios](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-material-comparison/README.md), with sensitive/passive splitting, the fixed palette and only the old total dotted reference on the new plot.
- [Matched sensitive-volume crossings versus eta](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-hit-comparison/README.md), with both stacked+total and individual-marker+total options.
- [Fatras truth-associated muon fits](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/fatras-baseline-comparison/README.md) at fixed pT 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV, 20,000 events per baseline/case, Bz=3 T, and an independent 50,000-event calibration for the current 2 mm response.

The evidence supports retaining the 2 mm working baseline with explicit tradeoffs: central d0 cores narrow while central relative-pT cores widen by about 6–13%. At forward 100 GeV the current core is narrower but full RMS is substantially larger. Material locality, one-phi-bin averaging, CSG conversion, simplified response and ideal truth seeds limit interpretation. The full-baseline comparison does not isolate pitch/service effects or establish pattern-recognition performance or engineering acceptance.

Validation: 32 focused tests pass; the map-record audit and all three plot replays pass. Separate PhysVal assessments reproduce the raw material, crossing and Fatras evidence at their named revisions. Hosted CI now runs the current comparison checks/replays. Reproduction recipes, compact binwise data and provenance are retained.

Per-PR [accounting coverage](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/baseline-material-comparison/interactions/pr-0113/accounting.md) and [interaction ledger](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/baseline-material-comparison/interactions/pr-0113.json) retain 13 selected counterless discussion sources, the four canonical journals, exposed agent roles and verified parent/child identities. Exact token counters are unavailable from the connected app; usage remains unknown, with no estimates or zeros substituted. The active publication turn is excluded from finalized usage.

Governing records: DES-025, DES-043, ADR-003. No geometry or runtime defaults change. This PR publishes qualified prototype characterization and is prepared for human review/merge.

Merge preparation: preserve the full commit history with a merge commit. Source-audit gates refer to the native execution/reduction SHAs retained in this branch.

Record the current 2 mm, reduced-service DES043 tracker material map and the old/new baseline comparisons used to assess the choice.

The retained map has **67 keyed portals and 8,650 averaged material bins**, bound to geometry `62f6056`, its compact/material/five factories, portal selection and exact map hashes. It was trained with 100,000 Geant4 geantinos and checked with 100,000 independent ACTS rays. The [map record](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-material-comparison/material-map-record.json) and [compressed map](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-material-comparison/material_map.json.gz) are included; full event samples remain local and ignored.

This PR also delivers:

- [Geant4 material stacks and ACTS ratios](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-material-comparison/README.md), with sensitive/passive splitting, the fixed palette and only the old total dotted reference on the new plot.
- [Matched sensitive-volume crossings versus eta](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/baseline-hit-comparison/README.md), with both stacked+total and individual-marker+total options.
- [Fatras truth-associated muon fits](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ee715547cb9d0f493502962566d87b0a2583a8b7/docs/validation/fatras-baseline-comparison/README.md) at fixed pT 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV, 20,000 events per baseline/case, Bz=3 T, and an independent 50,000-event calibration for the current 2 mm response.

The evidence supports retaining the 2 mm working baseline with explicit tradeoffs: central d0 cores narrow while central relative-pT cores widen by about 6–13%. At forward 100 GeV the current core is narrower but full RMS is substantially larger. Material locality, one-phi-bin averaging, CSG conversion, simplified response and ideal truth seeds limit interpretation. The full-baseline comparison does not isolate pitch/service effects or establish pattern-recognition performance or engineering acceptance.

Validation: 32 focused tests pass; the map-record audit and all three plot replays pass. Separate PhysVal assessments reproduce the raw material, crossing and Fatras evidence at their named revisions. Hosted CI now runs the current comparison checks/replays. Reproduction recipes, compact binwise data and provenance are retained.

Per-PR [accounting coverage](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/baseline-material-comparison/interactions/pr-0113/accounting.md) and [interaction ledger](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/baseline-material-comparison/interactions/pr-0113.json) retain 13 selected counterless discussion sources, the four canonical journals, exposed agent roles and verified parent/child identities. Exact token counters are unavailable from the connected app; usage remains unknown, with no estimates or zeros substituted. The active publication turn is excluded from finalized usage.

Governing records: DES-025, DES-043, ADR-003. No geometry or runtime defaults change. This PR publishes qualified prototype characterization and is prepared for human review/merge.

Merge preparation: preserve the full commit history with a merge commit. Source-audit gates refer to the native execution/reduction SHAs retained in this branch.
User, exact: “Now can you also run Fatras single muon resolutions 1, 5, 10, 100 comparing track parameters of old and new baseline - using truth tracking”.
